idiom_name: session-scoped state store + stateless render helpers (Streamlit st.session_state and the rerun model)
implementation_notes: In the data-app stack the container is the page function: it reads and writes st.session_state - a per-session store the framework keeps across reruns - and calls small render helpers that take plain values. Every interaction reruns the script from the top, so rendering is a pure function of the current session state and the helpers hold nothing themselves; a widget that declares a key has its value bound into session state automatically. For server-rendered web apps the same split is a view function plus a template partial that receives explicit context (Flask/Django), or a component object whose props are rendered; only hand-rolled desktop loops fall back to a plain model object plus a redraw.
code_sketch:
def render_lines(lines, on_remove):          # stateless child: values in, event out
    for line in lines:
        if st.button(f"remove {line['sku']}", key=f"rm-{line['sku']}"):
            on_remove(line["sku"])

def cart_page():                             # container: owns session state
    st.session_state.setdefault("lines", [])
    render_lines(st.session_state.lines, on_remove=remove_line)
pitfalls: Session state is tied to the WebSocket connection: a browser reload or a Markdown-link navigation resets it, and multipage apps share it, so it is not durable storage.

A widget's value cannot be set through session state after the widget was instantiated, and button-like widgets cannot be pre-set at all - initialize the key before creating the widget or mutate it in a callback.
Keeping per-user data in module-level globals instead of session state leaks it between users of the same server process.
